subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge: Resonance Disaster
description: One-minute skill: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge: Resonance Disaster.

hook.text: On November 7, 1940, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisted itself apart in a 40 mph wind. Footage of it is still stunning.

buildup.text: The bridge was unusually narrow and flexible. Wind pushed the deck sideways, and the deck pushed back. Oscillations grew.

discovery.text: Aeroelastic flutter — wind energy fed into the bridge's natural torsional frequency. Each cycle added energy instead of damping.

twist.text: The wind wasn't unusually strong. The bridge's shape caught wind like an airfoil, converting steady flow into twisting motion.

climax.text: Modern bridges use wind tunnel testing and tuned mass dampers. The Tacoma failure made aerodynamics a core part of bridge design.

punchline.text: The wind didn't push the bridge down. It taught it to dance until it broke.

quiz.question: What caused the Tacoma Narrows Bridge to collapse?
options: A sudden extreme wind gust snapped the main cables
Aeroelastic flutter fed wind energy into the bridge's natural frequency, amplifying oscillations
The concrete deck cracked from thermal expansion in the summer heat
